title: Seller trust microdeck for security stakeholders (WIP)
content:
Purpose: quick microdeck and seller playbook to surface trust evidence for security/compliance/IT stakeholders during pilot and procurement. Focus: short, skimmable artifacts an SE can drop in a meeting or email; leave room for customization.

Intended audience: Head of Security, Cloud Platform lead, Legal (Data Processing), Procurement technical reviewer, SRE. Primary ask: baseline trust + low-risk pilot.

Notes to self (tone): keep it evidence-first, avoid product jargon early — start with SLA/visibility/controls, then map to their risk model. Use 'private control plane' rather than product marketing names in initial slides.

Microdeck outline (3 slides — one-liner each + talking points)

Slide 1: "How Redwood reduces operational risk for LLM inference"
 - One line: predictable performance + explicit controls for data locality and auditing
 - Talking bullets: dedicated pools vs shared; VPC/private control plane options; KMS/HSM integrations for key separation; per-request audit logs; SLA targets and escalation path
 - Evidence callouts: customer anonymized case (finance vertical) reduced latency spikes with Dedicated; link to SLO docs (send after meeting)

Slide 2: "Visibility & control — what your security team can inspect"
 - One line: full telemetry + tamper-evident audit trails for inference requests
 - Talking bullets: token-level usage logs (redacted), trace IDs for request replay, model version pinning, RBAC and org-scoped API keys, audit retention windows (configurable), optional on-prem deployment for air-gapped needs
 - Appendix note: prepare screen share of Console -> Audit -> Request details for demo

Slide 3: "Pilot safety net & rollout guardrails"
 - One line: low-friction pilot with kill-switches, fallbacks, and measurable quality gates
 - Talking bullets: canary routing to smaller capacity; automatic fallback to simpler model variant on overload; prefix/KV caching opt-in to avoid repeated sensitive contexts; prompt watermarking recommendations for regulated data; post-deploy evaluation hooks and regression alerts
 - Ask: 30d pilot with explicit rollback criteria and a light SLA addendum

Quick 1-pager (to hand to procurement/IT) — language for SE to copy: 
 - Executive summary (2 sentences): Redwood offers a production-grade inference platform that can be run in your cloud or via a private control plane. We provide configurable data residency, KMS-backed encryption, and per-request audit logging to meet common enterprise controls.
 - Controls checklist (checkbox format):
   * Dedicated or private deployment option available
   * Customer-managed KMS / BYOK supported
   * Audit logs accessible with retention policy
   * Fine-grained RBAC + org scoping
   * SLA / uptime targets and credits clause (attach doc)
   * Compliance artifacts: SOC2 type II (in progress/available), penetration test summary available upon NDA
 - Next steps: 1) quick technical call (30m) with SRE and SE, 2) sandbox pilot details (capacity, data residency), 3) attach sample contract exhibit for pilot

Objection handling snippets (one-liners for quick use):
 - "We can't send production data": offer private control plane + local transformers package; propose synthetic data trial + redaction plan for first 2 weeks.
 - "We require full BYOK": confirm KMS/HSM integration and provide reference architecture diagram in follow-up.
 - "Latency spikes are a showstopper": discuss Dedicated pools and autoscale burst policy; offer latency percentiles from our telemetry for same-size pilots.

Technical appendix (bullets for SE prep):
 - Network: VPC peering, private link options, support for customer egress only, firewall IP ranges documented
 - Keys: customer-managed KMS or HSM; key rotation policies; no plaintext key storage in control plane
 - Data flow: inference request -> routing layer -> serving runtime -> optional cache -> response; logs emitted to customer log sinks (syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver) if configured
 - Hard guarantees: model version pinning prevents silent model swaps; rollout policies include canary, percentage traffic and time windows

Pilot checklist (practical steps to propose in pilot kickoff):
 1) Agree scope: sample endpoints, expected QPS, latency SLOs, sensitive data handling rules
 2) Deployment mode: hosted sandbox vs private control plane vs on-prem package
 3) Security review artifacts: architecture diagram, SOC/pen-test abstracts, KMS flow, data retention policy
 4) Observability plan: which dashboards + alerts we will expose, who gets read access
 5) Rollback criteria: error rate > X, latency p95 > Y ms for N minutes, data leakage concern -> immediate suspend
 6) Post-pilot evaluation: quality metrics by prompt set, cost per 1k tokens analysis, recommendation for Dedicated or full private rollout

Email/Slack template — short invite to a security reviewer: 
 "Hi <Name>,
We run a short independent checklist for security reviews of inference pilots. Can we do a 30m session this week to walk through architecture, KMS flow, and audit logs? We'll bring the SE + SRE and share a sandbox with controlled test data. —<SE name>"

Speaker notes + demo cues (for SE presenting):
 - Start with top-3 security asks: data residency, keys, and auditability
 - Share a live Console screenshot of audit events filtered by request id (redact customer ids)
 - Bring up fallback policy config to show kill-switch and canary toggles
 - If asked about compliance: acknowledge scope (SOC2 doc, in-house penetration test), offer next steps for deeper review under NDA

Open questions / follow-ups (todo):
 - Get updated pen-test summary from Security (Elena) — pending (Confluence link in artifacts)
 - Need a one-page architecture diagram variant for on-prem package (Marco owner)
 - Confirm SOC2 status and exact link we can share externally (legal sign-off)
 - Collect latency p95 numbers for Dedicated 4xA100 baseline (ops telemetry)

References & quick links to attach after meeting:
 - Console Audit docs (internal link)
 - Pilot contract exhibit template (legal draft link)
 - Internal playbook: how to spin a private control plane demo instance (ops runbook)

Small experiments to run (to iterate microdeck):
 - A/B two microdeck variants: one with compliance-first language and one with performance-first language; test CTO/HeadSec reaction in pilot sales cycle and note which opens conversation faster.
 - Create 1-page anonymized case study for a regulated customer (finance/health) showing timeline + mitigations.

Notes to collaborator reviewers: please push specific compliance links or numbers into the appendix rather than main slides. Keep slides light; main aim is to get to a technical walkthrough.

Last edited: quick sketch for SEs to use in calls. Will refine into a 3-slide PDF + 1-pg checklist for procurement once we validate language with legal.
